inst1: In front of you on the screen are four decks of cards labeled A, B, C, and D. You are completely free to choose a card from any deck, and you may continue choosing from the same deck or switch to another deck as often as you wish.After each card is selected, the amount of money you win or lose will be displayed in the information box above the decks. The computer will not tell you in advance how much money you will win or lose. You will gradually learn about the outcomes as you continue playing the game.
inst2: The goal of this game is to win as much money as possible while avoiding losing as much money as possible.An important hint is that the color of the cards has nothing to do with winning or losing. You will never be able to predict gains or losses based on the color of the cards.The only hint I can give you is that some decks are worse than others. No matter how much money you may have already lost, you still have a chance to finish with a profit if you stay away from the worst decks.Please treat this play money as if it were your own real money, and make every decision as though the money belonged to you.At the beginning of the game, the computer displays your principal (the money borrowed from the bank) in the red bar. This is the money you start with.When you win money, your bonus will increase and be displayed in the green bar above the principal. When you lose money, the computer will first deduct the loss from your bonus. If your bonus is insufficient, the remaining amount will be deducted from your principal.The text displayed above the card decks provides information about the outcome of each card you select.You will not know when the game will end. Simply continue playing until the computer displays a message indicating that the game is complete.
inst3: After the game is finished, you will be asked to complete a questionnaire related to the study.The experiment will then be complete.Thank you very much for your participation. Your help is greatly appreciated.
game_over: You've completed the task. Your net result is $
thank_you: Thank you for participating. Please wait for further instructions.
